decoder: Two mapped GF rates through frozen naive chess-cue-panel-v1 input-range calibration. Prefer lower clipped max score; exact ties choose A. Retain raw/signed/clipped signals and out-of-panel flags.
feedback: Experimental aversive contingency, counterbalanced across seed index and reversed after acquisition. These labels intentionally are NOT chess consequence scores. The encoder receives board/legal action/context only; no experimental target. Teacher presents cues and optional direct identified PPL103 stimulation, never parameter updates.
schedule: Alternate A/B in seed-parity order. Informative pulses follow experimental punished cue; absent has no pulse; shuffled independently permutes pulse sequence within phase at matched count; disabled gets informative pulses without local plasticity.
calibration: Keep the previously frozen naive input-domain reference identical for all new seeds and phases; never fit to observed learned choices. Out-of-panel saturation and any failed choices remain failures.
acceptance: Every informative seed must choose the newly safe cue after acquisition and reversal with positive target-signed margin changes. Reversal effects must exceed absent/shuffled controls under one-sided sign tests p<0.05. Require exact persistence/reset/restoration, disabled invariance, matched counts and fixed wiring/nonplastic state. All computational gates required; no retuning.
retention: Software efficacy persistence and repeat probes only, not measured biological retention.
scope: Independent encoder-seed association with overlapping real board-action descriptions. Same board/actions are reused: not unfamiliar chess-family transfer, verified chess feedback, full-model adaptation, Gate A biological validation or completed puzzle learning.
